content: 1. In 2010, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) supported a study on sodium intake. An expert provided opinions on population sodium intake to the US National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute's National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey Sodium Working Group in January 2011. Additionally, the expert advised on sodium intake measurement methods and their efficacy for the CDC's Epidemiology & Surveillance Branch during 2010–2011. 2. Dr. Lee Hooper disclosed receiving research funding from Barry Callebaut, directed to her university, to conduct a systematic review on the effects of chocolate and cocoa on markers of oxidative stress. This review was completed in August 2010. She also received funding from the Soy Nutrition Institute, again directed to her university, to perform a systematic review on the effects of soy and isoflavones on hormonal status in women, which was completed in July 2008. 3. Dr. Sarah Kelly declared receiving support for her participation in the third meeting of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health, provided by the local organizers of the meeting, specifically the KFDA/KHIDI. 4. Dr. Cho-il Kim stated that in 2009, she provided expert advice to the KFDA during the development of guidelines to identify energy-dense and nutrient-poor foods under the Special Act on Food Safety Management for Children. Since 2009, the sale of such foods has been prohibited within school premises and in designated stores near schools, known as the Green Food Zone. Additionally, since 2010, television advertisements for these foods have been banned between 5:00 PM and 7:00 PM daily. Dr. Kim noted the relevance of this information, as the regulations address the fat and sugar content of foods, which aligns with the NUGAG Subgroup's review of recommendations related to total fat and sugars. 5. Professor Paula Moynihan disclosed receiving a research grant, directed to her university, which included reviewing sugar intake in care homes as part of a larger dietary study funded by the UK Food Standards Agency/Department of Health. This study was completed in January 2011. She also declared that her travel costs for the third meeting of the NUGAG Subgroup on Diet and Health were covered by research funds from her university. 6. External experts and resource persons participated in discussions on the evidence during NUGAG meetings but did not vote on the recommendations. The final wording and determination of the strength of the recommendations were based solely on the consensus of NUGAG members. Members of the External Expert and Stakeholder Panel were required to submit a signed declaration of interests form and a current curriculum vitae before commenting on the draft recommendations and guideline document.
